title: A smooth quotient has a locally regular-sequence kernel
statement: Let $R\to A$ and $R\to C$ be smooth maps of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], let $\varphi:A\to C$ be a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism, and let $Q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ contain $\ker\varphi$. There exists $g\in A\setminus Q$ such that, in every model $D$ of the principal localization $A[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the extended ideal $(\ker\varphi)D$ is generated by a finite $D$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Tag 067T, lemma-immersion-lci-into-smooth-regular-immersion, smooth affine specialization, via Tag 063W(2).

proof.text: Put $I=\ker\varphi$. The induced algebra equivalence $A/I\simeq C$ gives smoothness of $A/I$. Both $A$ and $A/I$ are flat and finitely presented over $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. The surjection kernel is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg], using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra].

Contract $Q$ to $\mathfrak p$ in $R$ and let $P$ be its fibre prime. Write $F=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R A$, $J=IF$, $L=F_P$ and $K=JL$. We have $J\subseteq P$, hence $K\ne L$. The ring $L$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local]. Tensoring the quotient identifies $F/J$ with the smooth fibre of $A/I$. Localizing this quotient at the image of $P$ identifies its regular local ring with $L/K$, using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] and quotient localization. Smoothness over the residue field gives regularity of this quotient localization by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local], hence $L/K$ is regular local too.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to write $K$ as the ideal of a prefix of a parameter list of $L$. The full list is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. The prefix is weakly regular by the append criterion and lies in the maximal ideal, so it is regular. This includes a zero-length prefix.

Apply [lem-pur-flat-quotient-fiber-regular-sequence] to $R\to A$, $I$, and the fibre prime $P$. Its flatness, finite-presentation and finite-generation hypotheses hold by the first step, and its fibre-regularity hypothesis holds by the third. This gives the required principal neighbourhood and generators.
